Late-phase cuts are cheap only because the LR is near its floor and the averaging already dominates. Cuts that reach group 2 (half the MACs, most of the features) should cost more per second than the group-1 freeze did.

- whether the judge PCIe card penalizes bandwidth-bound levers;

forecasts.reason: Saves ~0.15 s on ~23 steps, but annealing group 2 from 75% perturbs the sensitive late end-point; expect a >0.1 pp loss.
No recipe change; I expect conv1 under 10% of step time because cuDNN already pads Cin=24, so H6.4.1 likely fails.
Removes ~11 steps (~0.23 s), which on the frontier costs ~0.15–0.2 pp, exceeding the 0.1 pp allowance.
cuDNN pads internally and conv1 is ~6% of MACs; padding adds 33% more conv1 FLOPs, so the net effect is ≤1%, short of 2%.

cruxes: Does a whole-train() profile (I071) show ≥5% GPU idle or host time outside the step graphs (per-epoch gather/interpolate/permute, the Python LR loop, Lookahead lerps)? That would be the only lever off the accuracy-time frontier.
Is E036's population mean really ≥0.753 (the pooled 20-seed unselected mean), or does every further cut need a real booster first? This decides whether any trim can pass the 40-seed bar.
Can the cuDNN/autotune kernel choices be pinned so rebuild noise (SD ~0.2 pp) stops deciding keeps? Without this, 3-seed gate results are mostly lottery.
